proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (>4 eV), electronically insulating Li-ion conductor that is chemically compatible with both sulfide Li6PS5Cl and the LiCoO2 cathode. Its phosphate chemistry is widely used as an interfacial buffer, so it should give a low interfacial penalty at 4.0 V and clear the 2.0 eV gap minimum.

LiF is a very wide-gap, electrochemically robust Li-ion insulator. Its fluoride anion is far less prone to redox or metathesis with the sulfide/chloride electrolyte than the oxide or phosphate anions that produced the P2O5/SO2/SCl4 contact products for Li3PO4. A LiF interlayer should therefore show a smaller contact penalty against Li6PS5Cl and LiCoO2 at 4.0 V while keeping the gap above 2 eV.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaaegs) gave a contact penalty of 0.337 eV/non-Li atom, with the electrolyte side reacting to P2O5, SCl4 and SO2 (bin 16, not acceptable). This suggests oxyanion coatings are chemically incompatible with the sulfide, so a halide family is the next test.

proposal.hypothesis: LiCl is a wide-gap Li-ion insulator (gap roughly 8 to 9 eV) whose anion matches the Cl in Li6PS5Cl. Chloride-chloride exchange should be thermodynamically mild, unlike the oxyanion and fluoride contacts that produced P2O5/SO2/SCl4 and LiPF6/S/SCl products. A chloride interlayer may therefore give a smaller contact penalty against the sulfide electrolyte at 4.0 V.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (penalty 0.337, bin 16) and LiF (penalty 0.310, bin 15) both failed through electrolyte-side reduction and metathesis products. The chloride anion is the only halide that already appears in the electrolyte, so it is a less disruptive test than the fluoride.
